text: Operator asked for a live Investigation Notes view (spec section 14) plus another evidence-collection pass. Starting by following up on the leads recorded in RUN-0001's notes: the three blocked Kempsey Shire Council pages (SRC-0010/0011/0012), the Level 2 water restrictions article, the PFAS article, and the 20 July 2026 Public Forum agenda.

Trying the Wayback Machine (web.archive.org) as an alternate route around the HTTP 403 block on SRC-0010 (Kempsey Council current-works page for the Willawarrin plant), since direct fetches are blocked regardless of headers used.

A Wayback Machine snapshot of SRC-0010 exists (dated 2025-07-08, confirmed via the archive.org availability API), and a HEAD request to it succeeds, but every GET attempt (with and without browser-style headers) returns HTTP 498. Not pursuing further workarounds - repeatedly varying request headers to force through a bot-detection block starts to cross from ordinary access into deliberate evasion, which this investigation should not do even for legitimate public-interest research. Logging this as a continued access gap rather than trying harder to defeat it.

Moving on to the other two unpursued leads noted in RUN-0001: The Macleay Argus 'Kempsey Shire moves to Level 2 water restrictions' (story 6198046) and Mirage News 'Kempsey Tap Water Passes Safety, Below PFAS Limits'. Checking both for relevance to the River conditions and Iron/Manganese contamination threads.

Both leads paid off. The Level 2 restrictions article is dated 4 June 2019 - five months earlier than the previously-earliest chronology entry (Oct 2019) - and names Willawarrin and Bellbrook among the affected supply schemes, pushing the known drought onset back. The PFAS article (Mirage News, 5 Feb 2025) names Bellbrook specifically as one of eight systems tested and passing PFAS screening - the first Bellbrook-specific evidence found since the 2020 restoration. Preserving both now as EV-0009 and EV-0010.

This run's findings are now recorded: EV-0009 and EV-0010 added to the Evidence Register, CHR-0007 added to the Chronology, THR-01/THR-05/THR-14 updated, RUN-0002 logged in the Automation Log, SRCH-0006 logged in the Search Log, and DEC-0006 recorded for the decision to stop at the Wayback Machine block. The 20 July 2026 Public Forum agenda and the three blocked Kempsey Council pages remain open leads for a future run with manual browser access. Validating and committing now.

Operator asked to continue with RUN-0003 and gave the operator the four blocked kempsey.nsw.gov.au URLs (SRC-0010, SRC-0011, SRC-0012, and the 20 July 2026 Public Forum agenda) to try from their own browser tools. Not re-attempting those myself (see DEC-0006). Starting this run on new angles instead: NSW tender/contract-award records for the LC Water contract (Q-0003/Q-0004), NSW Electoral Commission records for the Kempsey mayoral change (Q-0004), and the WaterNSW 2025 compliance report noticed but not yet fetched in RUN-0001's search results.

Found two Macleay Argus articles confirming the Kempsey mayoral transition: Leo Hauville (outgoing) to Kinne Ring (53.67% after preferences, preliminary result 30 Sep 2024, sworn in 9 Oct 2024). This resolves Q-0004. However, the swearing-in article's own text states results were 'for the September 9, 2024 Local Government election' - but 9 September 2024 was a Monday, and multiple independent sources confirm the 2024 NSW Local Government elections were held statewide on Saturday 14 September 2024. Tried to find a citable, fetchable source stating the 14th explicitly to properly evidence both sides of this as a Contradiction Register entry, but elections.nsw.gov.au, campbelltown.nsw.gov.au, and sah.org.au all blocked the request (the last via an Incapsula bot challenge) - not pursuing further per DEC-0006. Recording this as a new open question instead of a contradiction, since I only have one-sided evidence for the discrepancy.

Q-0004 closed (EV-0011, EV-0012), THR-15 marked Complete, and Q-0006 opened for the residual date discrepancy. Moving on to Q-0003 (cost increase) and Q-0005 (main plant contractor): checking the WaterNSW 2025 compliance report noticed in RUN-0001's search results, and searching for LC Water / Willawarrin tender or contract-award records.

Found an earlier origin point for the Willawarrin plant: a 17 May 2022 Kempsey Shire Council press release (via Mirage News and National Tribune, identical content) announcing a $54 million water and sewer budget that already names Willawarrin as one of two new water treatment plant locations, and mentions a separate 'emergency water treatment plant' installed at Steuart McIntyre Dam for the main Kempsey/Lower Macleay supply. This pushes the documented project history back over two years before the Aug 2024 '$4m, nearing tender' article. A second Pump Industry Magazine article on the tender stage exists but pumpindustry.com.au is blocked (same as SRC-0009) - registering it as a known-but-inaccessible source rather than pursuing it further.

Fetched and full-text searched the WaterNSW 2025 compliance report (parliament.nsw.gov.au, 12.5MB PDF) for Willawarrin, Bellbrook, Kempsey, and Macleay - zero mentions of any of them. Ruling this source out: Willawarrin's supply is run directly by Kempsey Shire Council (bores/river), not one of WaterNSW's regulated schemes, so this report isn't relevant to this case. Not registering it as a source, since it was checked and found not to apply - recording the negative result here instead, consistent with the 'No Change Detected' principle.

Re-checked for any new commissioning-status update on the Willawarrin plant (Q-0001) with fresh search phrasing - nothing beyond what's already registered. Confirms the only remaining path to Q-0001 is the blocked Kempsey Council pages, which the operator is now trying via their own browser tools. Wrapping up RUN-0003: closed Q-0004, opened Q-0006, added EV-0011 through EV-0013, CHR-0008 through CHR-0011, and SRC-0016 through SRC-0022 (three of the new sources are further access gaps, honestly logged rather than forced through). Validating and committing now.

Reconciliation: a separate, earlier evidence-collection pass (also self-identified as 'RUN-0003') was carried out in parallel on an unmerged branch, before this repository's actual RUN-0003 (above, CHG-0007) was committed to main. Both independently investigated the same Kempsey mayoral transition for Q-0004. This repository's committed RUN-0003 has the stronger evidentiary basis - EV-0011/EV-0012 are Verified, preserved, and hashed, against a source-search-snippet-only, Requires Verification finding on the other branch - so that branch's mayoral evidence (its own EV-0011, a chronology entry, and a thread update) is being dropped as redundant/superseded rather than merged. This run (RUN-0004) instead carries forward only what that branch found that remains genuinely new: two source registrations (the 20 July 2026 Council Public Forum page, and a tender listing for the Steuart McIntyre Dam plant) and a decision not to accept an unverified 'Bellbrook Water Treatment Plant' claim as evidence (DEC-0007), which this repository's own EV-0013 does not corroborate either.

Registered SRC-0023 (Kempsey Shire Council Public Forum, 20 July 2026 - confirmed to exist via search indexing, but blocked to fetch like SRC-0010/0011/0012/0021/0022) and SRC-0024 (Australian Tenders listing for the Steuart McIntyre Dam Water Treatment Plant Design & Construction tender - confirms a tender process occurred for Q-0005's still-unnamed contractor, but the listing itself is also blocked). Updated THR-08 and THR-13's outstanding_work to reference both. No new evidence items added - neither source added a fact beyond 'this exists and is blocked', which doesn't clear the bar for a register entry on its own.

RUN-0004 recorded: SRC-0023/SRC-0024 added, SRCH-0013 through SRCH-0016 logged (consolidating the other branch's searches for Q-0001/Q-0002/Q-0003/Q-0005/the Public Forum lead - all 'no relevant change' except the two new sources above), DEC-0007 recorded. No evidence, chronology, or open-question changes - Q-0001, Q-0002, Q-0003, and Q-0005 remain open with no new facts found this run beyond the two access-gap sources. Validating and committing now.

Operator asked to continue evidence collection (RUN-0005). Targeting the four still-open questions: Q-0001 (commissioning status), Q-0002 (Bellbrook-specific infrastructure), Q-0003 (cost increase reason), Q-0005 (Steuart McIntyre Dam contractor).

This session's fetch tool returns HTTP 403 Forbidden on every URL attempted, including domains this repository has previously fetched and preserved successfully from other sessions (miragenews.com - the exact SRC-0015/EV-0010 URL), and even on completely unrelated control URLs (en.wikipedia.org, example.com). This is a session-level tooling constraint, not a site-specific bot-detection block like DEC-0006's - recording as DEC-0008 so a future session doesn't mistake this run's lower yield for an absence of available sources. No source can be preserved or hashed by this session as a result; any new lead found via search this run is registered as a Source only, not promoted to an Evidence Register entry, since this repository's own bar (a real preserved/hashed file) can't be met right now.

Two independent search queries ('Steuart McIntyre Dam water treatment plant contractor awarded construction company' and a follow-up naming-check query) both returned consistent wording identifying the Q-0005 contractor as 'LC Eire, a partnership between LC Water and Eire Constructions', apparently drawn from Utility Magazine's 'Work begins on $52.9M NSW water project' and a Mirage News article on the same $52.9m package. Could not fetch either article directly to confirm the primary text or get a direct quotation (see NOTE-0017). Registering both as new, blocked sources (SRC-0025, SRC-0026) and updating Q-0005/THR-13's outstanding_work to record this as a strong, cross-confirmed-by-search-summary lead that still requires primary-source confirmation before it can become an Evidence Register entry.

Also searched for Q-0003 (cost increase reason) and Q-0002/THR-14 (Bellbrook-specific infrastructure) with fresh phrasing. Nothing new on Q-0003 beyond what SRC-0021/SRC-0022 already flag. One search's own summary asserted a distinct '$270 million' water/sewer program and a named 'Bellbrook Water Treatment Plant' - a second, independent query did not reproduce either figure, and the 'Bellbrook Water Treatment Plant' claim is the same unverified, self-contradicting assertion DEC-0007 already declined to accept. Not re-litigating that decision: still no evidence of a dedicated Bellbrook treatment plant. Also re-checked Q-0001 (commissioning) with date-bounded phrasing ('since April 2026') - no source dated after March 2025 found; the 'early 2026' target remains the most recent status anywhere in reach of this session's tools.

RUN-0005 wrapping up: SRC-0025/SRC-0026 added, SRCH-0017 through SRCH-0022 logged, DEC-0008 recorded. No Evidence Register, Chronology, or Open Question changes this run - Q-0001, Q-0002, Q-0003, and Q-0005 remain open. THR-13's outstanding_work updated with the LC Eire lead. Validating and committing now.

Operator asked to continue (RUN-0006). Re-testing whether last run's fetch-tool outage (DEC-0008) was transient before starting fresh searches on Q-0001, Q-0002, Q-0003, and a new angle: the Thunggutti Aboriginal Community's water-security status, which EV-0010 already names as one of the eight tested supply systems but which has no dedicated thread yet.

Retried fetching the exact SRC-0026 URL from RUN-0005 - still HTTP 403 Forbidden. DEC-0008's constraint still applies this session; not retrying further per that decision. Continuing with search-only research.

Two independent search queries ('Thunggutti Aboriginal Community Bellbrook water supply security drinking water' and a follow-up on the specific program name) both surfaced NSW's 'Aboriginal Communities Water and Sewerage Program' (a $200 million joint NSW Government/NSW Aboriginal Land Council initiative running since December 2008) and both consistently state its Completed Projects listing names Bellbrook as a community that has received drinking-water and sewerage upgrade/repair work. Neither search surfaced a date or scope of work more specific than 'completed'. This is a genuinely new, substantive lead for Q-0002/THR-14 (Bellbrook-specific infrastructure, open since RUN-0001) - a dedicated program distinct from the Willawarrin plant. Could not fetch the program's own completed-projects page to confirm (water.dcceew.nsw.gov.au, same domain family as the already-blocked SRC-0006/SRC-0007). Registering as a new, blocked source (SRC-0027) rather than an Evidence Register entry, consistent with DEC-0008.

Re-checked Q-0001 (commissioning) and Q-0003 (cost increase reason) with fresh phrasing - both returned only already-registered facts ('early 2026' target, the $4m-to-$8m figures with no stated reason). No new sources for either this run.

RUN-0006 wrapping up: SRC-0027 added, SRCH-0023 through SRCH-0026 logged. No Evidence Register, Chronology, or Open Question status changes - Q-0001, Q-0002, Q-0003, and Q-0005 remain open, but Q-0002/THR-14's outstanding_work now points to a specific, named program (Aboriginal Communities Water and Sewerage Program) as the next thing to confirm, rather than an open-ended gap. Validating and committing now.

Operator asked to continue (RUN-0007). Retried fetching SRC-0027's URL - still HTTP 403 (DEC-0008 unchanged). Searched Q-0001, Q-0002, and Q-0003 with fresh phrasing: a Bellbrook-specific ACWSP completion-date/scope query (third independent search reproducing the same bare fact as NOTE-0023, no new detail), a Willawarrin community-update date search (Spring 2025/Summer 2026 - nothing dated after the already-registered Autumn 2025 update), and two NSW Safe and Secure Water Program project-status searches (aggregate program-wide figures only, no Willawarrin-specific completion status).

RUN-0007 wrapping up: no new sources, evidence, chronology, or open-question changes. Everything found this run either reproduced already-registered facts or added no new detail to an already-open lead. Logging as 'No relevant change detected.' per spec section 7, rather than padding the register with restatements. Q-0001, Q-0002, Q-0003, and Q-0005 remain open. Validating and committing the logs now.

Operator asked to continue (RUN-0008). Retried the fetch tool once (a Macleay Argus URL) - still HTTP 403, DEC-0008 unchanged. Before running fresh searches, re-read the existing Evidence Register closely for anything already on file that hadn't been cross-checked against itself.

Found an internal contradiction that required no new fetch to identify: EV-0005 (water.nsw.gov.au, 21 March 2025) states the Willawarrin plant serves 'the village's 130 residents', while EV-0006 (water.dcceew.nsw.gov.au, 24 March 2025) - three days later, describing the same project - states 'Willawarrin (population 180)'. Both are NSW Government primary sources already Verified and preserved in this register; neither had been checked against the other. Recording as CTR-0001, the Contradiction Register's first entry.

Searched for specific ADWG iron/manganese concentration figures (mg/L) for Willawarrin/Bellbrook (THR-03/THR-04's stated gap) and for any pre-2019 history of water quality problems (THR-01's stated gap). Neither search surfaced numeric concentration data or pre-2019 history beyond what's already registered - both remain genuine, unfilled gaps.

A tangential lead surfaced while searching: a seven-year (2016-2023) Save Our Macleay River / Southern Cross University citizen-science study found arsenic and antimony from historic Hillgrove mining tailings persisting in the Macleay River catchment (Bakers Creek). This concerns a different contaminant (arsenic/antimony, not iron/manganese) from an upstream historic mining source, and it is not yet established whether it bears on Willawarrin or Bellbrook's own supply specifically rather than the broader catchment. Registered as SRC-0028 (fetch-blocked) for completeness, deliberately not linked to any thread or treated as case-relevant evidence without further confirmation - avoiding scope creep into a wider catchment-contamination story this case's own geographic_scope (Willawarrin and Bellbrook specifically) does not cover.

RUN-0008 wrapping up: CTR-0001 added (Contradiction Register's first entry), SRC-0028 added, SRCH-0031/SRCH-0032 logged. No Evidence Register or Chronology changes. Q-0001, Q-0002, Q-0003, and Q-0005 remain open; THR-03/THR-04's concentration-data gap and THR-01's pre-2019 history gap remain unfilled. Validating and committing now.

Operator asked to continue (RUN-0009). Retried the fetch tool once - still HTTP 403, DEC-0008 unchanged. Tried three fresh angles not attempted in prior runs: federal Member for Cowper Pat Conaghan's own statements/website (Q-0001/Q-0003), the 'Your Say Macleay' community engagement platform's Willawarrin page (Q-0001), and a direct delay/pushed-back search given how far past the 'early 2026' target the current date (28 July 2026) now is.

All three angles reproduced only already-registered facts (LC Water as contractor, the March 2025 construction start, 'early 2026' target) or unrelated results. No new sources, evidence, chronology, or open-question changes this run - logging as 'No relevant change detected.' per spec section 7. Q-0001, Q-0002, Q-0003, Q-0005, and Q-0006 remain open. Validating and committing the logs now.

Operator asked to continue (RUN-0010). Retried the fetch tool against a URL already preserved successfully in an earlier session (EV-0010's miragenews.com URL) plus a control URL (en.wikipedia.org) - both still HTTP 403. DEC-0008's session-level fetch outage remains in effect. Picking three angles not yet tried in RUN-0005 through RUN-0009: (1) whether SRC-0028's Hillgrove mining contamination has any specific link to Willawarrin/Bellbrook's own extraction points rather than the general catchment, (2) a direct NSW Electoral Commission search for Q-0006's disputed election date, (3) an ABS Census search for CTR-0001's disputed population figure.

SRC-0028 follow-up: found nothing tying Hillgrove/Bakers Creek arsenic-antimony contamination specifically to Willawarrin's own bore/river extraction points - only general catchment-wide references (the dispersion train runs ~50km downstream of Hillgrove, described as reaching the Macleay floodplain generally). Confirms the prior run's caution was correct: this stays unlinked to any thread, avoiding scope creep beyond this case's Willawarrin/Bellbrook focus.

Strong lead for Q-0006: multiple independent search-engine snippets, including one referencing an NSW Electoral Commission media release specifically about Kempsey (alongside Shellharbour Ward A and Singleton), consistently state Kempsey Shire Council's 2024 election day was Saturday 14 September 2024 - not the 9 September 2024 date EV-0011 attributed to the result. Most likely explanation: EV-0011's '9' is a transcription error for '14', matching the statewide polling day. Registered as SRC-0029, but not promoted to evidence or used to close Q-0006, since nothing could be fetched or preserved this session (DEC-0008).

Strong lead for CTR-0001: the ABS 2021 Census QuickStats for Willawarrin (SAL14312) gives a population of 183, close to EV-0006's 180 figure and well above EV-0005's 130 figure - suggesting 130 is the outlier needing correction, not 180. Registered as SRC-0030, but not used to resolve CTR-0001 (still Open), since nothing could be fetched or preserved this session (DEC-0008).

RUN-0010 wrapping up: SRC-0029 and SRC-0030 added (strong, specific leads for Q-0006 and CTR-0001 respectively, both fetch-blocked this session per DEC-0008), SRCH-0036 through SRCH-0041 logged. No Evidence Register, Chronology, or Open Question/Contradiction status changes - Q-0001, Q-0002, Q-0003, Q-0005, Q-0006, and CTR-0001 all remain open, but two of them now have a specific, named primary source a future run with working fetch access should check first. Validating and committing now.

Operator asked to continue (RUN-0011). Found on pulling that a parallel run had already landed as RUN-0010 (SRC-0028/0029/0030) since this session last pushed. Reviewed its findings before doing new work, to avoid duplicating the same searches. Taking a different approach this run: rather than more WebSearch on already-well-covered ground, tried a pure computation the fetch outage can't block - checking what day of the week 9 September 2024 and 14 September 2024 actually fell on (Q-0006's disputed election date), since this is a deterministic calendar fact requiring no external source at all.

Computed directly: 9 September 2024 was a Monday; 14 September 2024 was a Saturday. This alone already made EV-0011's '9 September' date implausible (NSW council elections are conventionally held on Saturdays), but a follow-up search found the specific statutory basis: NSW ordinary council elections are legally required to fall on 'the second Saturday in September' (Local Government Act 1993/Local Government (General) Regulation 2021). Checking the calendar: the Saturdays in September 2024 were the 7th, 14th, 21st, and 28th - so 14 September was specifically the second Saturday, matching the statute exactly, while 9 September was neither a Saturday nor a plausible alternative reading. Registered the statute as SRC-0031 (fetch-blocked, see DEC-0008) and strengthened Q-0006 with this reasoning - not closing the question, since a real preserved primary citation is still required and remains blocked, but this is now about as strong a non-primary-source case as this investigation can build.

RUN-0011 wrapping up: SRC-0031 added, Q-0006 strengthened with independently-computed calendar facts plus a statutory citation, SRCH-0042 logged. No Evidence Register, Chronology, or Contradiction changes - Q-0001 through Q-0006 and CTR-0001 all remain formally open pending fetch access, but Q-0006 now has the strongest non-primary-source case this investigation can build without a working fetch tool. Validating and committing now.

Operator asked to continue (RUN-0012). No parallel commits since this session's last push. Retried the fetch tool against SRC-0031's URL - still HTTP 403, DEC-0008 unchanged. Searched THR-13's stated gap (the Steuart McIntyre Dam plant's contractor and construction progress) with fresh phrasing focused on the dam's own history and the project's construction status.

Found a genuinely new event not previously registered: two independent articles (an NSW Government release and a Port Macquarie News/Macleay Argus syndicated report) both describe a sod-turning/ground-breaking event for the Steuart McIntyre Dam plant, placed 'as of July 2025' - consistent with EV-0005's announced mid-2025 construction start, and the equivalent milestone to EV-0006 for the Willawarrin plant. Neither names the contractor (Q-0005 remains open), but this confirms construction is genuinely underway rather than only funded/announced. Registered as SRC-0032 (NSW Government, primary) and SRC-0033 (independent media corroboration) - both fetch-blocked this session (DEC-0008) - and updated THR-13's outstanding_work accordingly.

RUN-0012 wrapping up: SRC-0032/SRC-0033 added, THR-13 updated, SRCH-0043/SRCH-0044 logged. No Evidence Register, Chronology, Open Question, or Contradiction status changes - all remain open, though THR-13 now records a confirmed construction-start milestone. Validating and committing now.

Operator asked to continue (RUN-0013). Retried the fetch tool once (SRC-0032's URL) - still HTTP 403, DEC-0008 unchanged. Tried the 'Your Say Macleay' Willawarrin quick-poll results sub-page (a specific URL not tried in RUN-0009's check of the parent page) and NSW Health's Drinking Water Database/Data Portal for THR-03/THR-04's stated concentration-data gap.

The quick-poll page returned no usable detail via search snippet (only generic Willawarrin background copy). The Drinking Water Database angle initially looked promising - one search summary claimed 'both Willawarrin and Bellbrook water supplies showed 100% compliance across major parameters' for 2023-2024 - but two follow-up searches attributed the actual numeric figures (98.3% pH compliance, 176 samples, etc.) specifically to 'Kempsey and Lower Macleay Water Supply' and 'South West Rocks Water Supply', with no Willawarrin-specific table surfacing at all. This is the same unreliable, self-contradicting search-summary pattern DEC-0007 already declined to accept - not registering any of this as evidence or even as a new source, since it isn't clear enough which system the figures actually describe to be worth citing even provisionally.

RUN-0013 wrapping up: no new sources, evidence, chronology, or open-question changes. Both angles this run either returned nothing usable or produced an inconsistent search summary not solid enough to register even as a source, consistent with DEC-0007's standard. Logging as 'No relevant change detected.' Q-0001 through Q-0006 and CTR-0001 all remain open. Validating and committing the logs now.

Operator asked to continue (RUN-0014). Retried the fetch tool once (an ABS Census URL) - still HTTP 403, DEC-0008 unchanged. Tried a genuinely unexplored avenue this run: Bellbrook's own general history and background, rather than more Willawarrin-plant-focused searches, on the reasoning that this register has almost no Bellbrook-specific context at all beyond its water supply status.

Two independent search queries both returned consistent, specific figures for Bellbrook: gazetted in 1892 (named for bellbirds along Nulla Nulla Creek), registered with the National Trust of Australia in 1978 and the Register of the National Estate in 1981 as a heritage timber-industry village, and a 2021 Census population of 339 (up 21% from 273 in 2016) - a different ABS State Suburb code (SAL10270) from Willawarrin's (SAL14312, already SRC-0030). This fills a real gap: no Bellbrook-specific historical or population data existed in this register before. Registered as SRC-0034 (Wikipedia) and SRC-0035 (ABS QuickStats), both fetch-blocked this session (DEC-0008), and added as general background context to THR-14 rather than as evidence of the town's water infrastructure status specifically.

RUN-0014 wrapping up: SRC-0034/SRC-0035 added, THR-14 updated with Bellbrook's general background, SRCH-0047/SRCH-0048 logged. No Evidence Register, Chronology, Open Question, or Contradiction changes. Validating and committing now.

Operator asked to continue (RUN-0015). Retried the fetch tool once (a Wikipedia URL) - still HTTP 403, DEC-0008 unchanged. Applied RUN-0014's same approach to the other town: searched for Willawarrin's own general history and background (THR-01's stated gap), rather than more plant-status searches.

First search confirmed the already-known 183 population figure (corroborating SRC-0030) plus general tourism context (Slim Dusty Way Scenic Drive) - too thin to register on its own. A follow-up search found something more substantive: Kempsey Shire Council's own heritage library page, 'Early history of Willawarrin', cross-confirmed across two independent queries with consistent facts - part of the Toorooka pastoral lease from 1842, first hotel built 1893, an important livestock-selling centre 1949-1970. This is general settlement history, not water-specific, but is a genuinely new, council-sourced historical record - the earliest documented history found for Willawarrin by over a century. Registered as SRC-0036 (fetch-blocked, DEC-0008) and added to THR-01.

RUN-0015 wrapping up: SRC-0036 added, THR-01 updated, SRCH-0049/SRCH-0050 logged. No Evidence Register, Chronology, Open Question, or Contradiction changes - the pre-2019 water-quality-specific gap in THR-01 remains open even though general settlement history is now on file. Validating and committing now.

Operator asked to continue (RUN-0016). Retried the fetch tool once (SRC-0036's URL) - still HTTP 403, DEC-0008 unchanged. Searched for the exact date Bellbrook's trucked-water period began (THR-02's stated gap: whether Bellbrook actually needed trucked water on EV-0001's anticipated 'within a week' timeline).

The first search surfaced something more significant than the trucked-water date itself: Bellbrook was evacuated due to the Carrai East Bushfire in November 2019. A follow-up search cross-confirmed and substantially detailed this, with specific, consistent, named facts: the fire accelerated 8 November 2019 amid extreme dry/windy conditions (2019 was Kempsey's driest year on record, per RFS Superintendent Lachlann Ison); Bellbrook Public School (principal Allison Mitchell) became an evacuation centre on 11 November 2019, sheltering approximately 120 people plus pets and livestock, as the fire destroyed homes and properties in the Bellbrook/Willawarrin area. This is very likely the specific bushfire event behind EV-0002/EV-0003's cited cause ('drought, bushfire, and subsequent heavy rainfall'), and fills a real gap between CHR-0007 (June 2019) and CHR-0001 (late October 2019). Registered as SRC-0037 (fetch-blocked, DEC-0008) - not yet promotable to Evidence/Chronology since Chronology entries require a real evidence_id and nothing could be preserved this session.

RUN-0016 wrapping up: SRC-0037 added, THR-01 updated with the Carrai East Bushfire finding, SRCH-0051/SRCH-0052 logged. No Evidence Register or Chronology changes this run (the bar for a Chronology entry - a real evidence_id - can't be met while the fetch tool is down), but this is one of the strongest unpromoted leads in the register: a specific, dated, well-corroborated event that would likely become its own Chronology entry the moment a working fetch tool is available. Validating and committing now.

Operator asked to continue (RUN-0017). Retried the fetch tool against abc.net.au (a domain not tried before) - got a different error ('Claude Code is unable to fetch from www.abc.net.au') rather than the usual HTTP 403, but still no content retrieved. Looked for further, independent corroboration of RUN-0016's Carrai East Bushfire finding (SRC-0037) rather than a wholly new angle, since it's the strongest unpromoted lead currently in the register.

Found a third independent source: the NSW Department of Education's own December 2019 article 'In the eye of the firestorm', reproducing SRC-0037's core facts (principal Allison Mitchell, ~120 people plus animals sheltered at Bellbrook Public School on 11 November 2019) with an added, specific detail - the school lost power and phone lines by 11:30pm that night, with the fire visible approaching from behind the building. This is closer in time to the event (Dec 2019) than SRC-0037's one-year retrospective, and comes from a government department rather than media/RFS sources - meaningfully strengthens the finding. Registered as SRC-0038 (fetch-blocked, DEC-0008).

RUN-0017 wrapping up: SRC-0038 added, SRC-0037's availability_notes updated to reference the new corroboration, SRCH-0053/SRCH-0054 logged. No Evidence Register or Chronology changes - the Carrai East Bushfire finding is now backed by three independent sources but still can't be promoted without a working fetch tool. Validating and committing now.

Operator asked to continue (RUN-0018). Retried the fetch tool once (SRC-0038's URL) - still HTTP 403, DEC-0008 unchanged. Did an internal cross-reference pass over the existing Evidence Register (the approach that found CTR-0001) looking for anything else unexploited: checked EV-0001's '80% and falling, 1,900 ML remaining' dam figures against EV-0005's '2,500 ML capacity' (80% of 2,500 would be 2,000 ML, not 1,900) - judged this too soft to register as a contradiction, since both figures in EV-0001 are already self-qualified as approximate ('approximately 80%') within a single article, unlike CTR-0001's two separately-published, unqualified figures.

Also searched THR-06's stated gap (why Willawarrin's bore/river supply was never connected to the more secure Steuart McIntyre Dam/Sherwood Borefield network). The only result confirmed Sherwood Borefield's distance from the dam (2km) but not from Willawarrin, and its own summary conflated the two separate plants again (attributing the Steuart McIntyre Dam project's pipeline/pump work to 'a new $8 million water treatment plant at Willawarrin') - the same unreliable-summary pattern already declined per DEC-0007.
